author: reek
body: A child widget must render IN FRONT of its parent, and a gauge's fill in front of its own track.

author: reek
body: The rasterizer keeps a pixel only if its depth is strictly less than the one already stored, so geometry drawn at the depth of a fill that already covers it is discarded. Draw a whole widget tree at one depth and only the root survives. Nothing in the triangle count can see this: the losing rects are submitted and counted exactly as the winning ones are, which is why the GuiOS desktop reported twenty-two triangles a frame while painting nothing but its own background. The instrument has to read pixels.

author: reek
body: So this renders a panel containing a separator and a gauge, then counts framebuffer pixels of each child's colour. The panel paints pal-bg, the separator pal-border, the gauge fill pal-primary -- three distinct values in theme-terminal, which is what makes the children legible against their parent. Both counts are ZERO when the depth rule is broken, and the test was run against a compiler without the fix to confirm exactly that.

author: reek
body: The scan strides eight columns and every row: a separator is one pixel tall and spans nearly the full width, so a column stride finds it and a row stride could miss it. Counting is deliberate rather than sampling one computed coordinate -- it does not have to know where layout put anything, so it stays honest when the layout changes.
